periods.analysis: We are carrying the demand of a gateway airport, but we are not yet delivering the reliability Harborview passengers deserve. Annual enplaned passengers stand at 16,742,306, still below the 18,000,000 target, while on-time performance is red at 73.5% against an 80% standard. Peak TSA/CBP wait time is 24 minutes, four minutes over target, with the worst pressure showing on the early-morning international bank at Concourse C and the 1500-1800 domestic departures on the north checkpoint. The bright spot is commercial discipline: non-aeronautical revenue per enplanement is green at $11.99, helped by the Gate B12 market hall opening and stronger garage pre-booking.
periods.recommendations: Stand up a daily 0630 Airport Reliability Huddle with airlines, TSA, CBP, ground handlers, and Airfield Ops to work the top delay codes flight by flight, not in generalities. Add two temporary queue marshals at North Checkpoint and trial dynamic lane assignments for the Concourse C international arrivals bank. Sustain the green revenue result by extending garage pre-booking offers to the airport app and protecting dwell-time concessions during construction phasing.

periods.analysis: The quarter moved in the wrong direction on the two measures that define the passenger experience. Annual enplaned passengers improved by 812,783, from 16,742,306 to 17,555,089, but remained yellow and short of the 18,000,000 target. On-time performance slipped from 73.5% to 73%, still red, and TSA/CBP peak wait time deteriorated from 24 minutes to 29 minutes as holiday loads collided with CBP booth outages in Federal Inspection Station lanes 7-10. Non-aeronautical revenue per enplanement rose from $11.99 to $12.50, green, showing the terminal can earn even while operations are under strain.
periods.recommendations: Treat the 29-minute peak wait as a control failure and publish a holiday after-action roster by checkpoint, booth, and shift before the January schedule build. Require the three largest carriers to submit turn-time recovery plans for the late-arriving evening narrowbody bank, including tow crew coverage and gate-readiness timestamps. Sustain the $12.50 revenue performance by keeping the pop-up retail program in Gates A4-A8 through spring break, but do not allow concession deliveries to block passenger circulation at peak.

periods.analysis: Passenger demand finally cleared the line: annual enplaned passengers increased by 924,152, from 17,555,089 to 18,479,241, and is now green above the 18,000,000 target. That growth exposed the weak seam in the operation, because on-time performance fell again from 73% to 72.4%, red, and TSA/CBP peak wait time worsened from 29 minutes to 32 minutes, also red. The longest queues were tied to Sunday international arrivals and the 0500-0730 checkpoint surge, with CT-3 at South Checkpoint and CBP primary booth 12 both out of service during parts of the quarter. Non-aeronautical revenue per enplanement eased from $12.50 to $12.07 but stayed green and comfortably above the $10.50 target.
periods.recommendations: Keep the growth, but put the operation on a recovery footing: assign an incident commander for the first departure wave every Friday-Monday until on-time performance is back above 75%. Work with TSA to accelerate CT-3 maintenance and open a dedicated crew-member/family lane during the 0500-0730 surge to protect throughput. Sustain revenue by renewing the high-performing local food-and-beverage carts in Concourse B, while using lease language to require off-peak stocking windows.

periods.analysis: This quarter confirms that the Q1 growth was not yet a stable operating model. Annual enplaned passengers dropped by 1,043,191, from 18,479,241 to 17,436,050, moving back to yellow and below the 18,000,000 target. On-time performance declined from 72.4% to 71.8%, still red, while TSA/CBP peak wait improved from 32 minutes to 29 minutes but remained above the 20-minute target. Non-aeronautical revenue per enplanement softened from $12.07 to $11.89, still green, with parking holding up better than in-terminal spend during the shoulder-season schedule reduction.
periods.recommendations: Move from diagnosis to intervention by launching a 90-day Turn Zero program on the first 40 daily departures, with gate-ready, crew-ready, and bag-ready timestamps owned by the Airport Operations Center. Keep the TSA/CBP wait-time recovery going by redeploying the temporary queue team to South Checkpoint and publishing hourly lane utilization to TSA leadership. Sustain the green revenue line by bundling parking reservations with airline confirmation emails for summer travel, and target concession promotions to the lower-spend midday window.

periods.analysis: We saw modest relief at the checkpoints, but the airfield and gate operation continued to slide. Annual enplaned passengers decreased by 917,564, from 17,436,050 to 16,518,486, remaining yellow and well below the 18,000,000 target. On-time performance moved down from 71.8% to 71.5%, red, with recurring delay clusters on Taxiway Kilo closures and late aircraft swaps at Gates D2-D6. TSA/CBP peak wait time improved from 29 minutes to 25 minutes, still yellow, and non-aeronautical revenue per enplanement edged up from $11.89 to $12.02, green, helped by summer parking yield and the Pier 3 cruise-transfer retail package.
periods.recommendations: Lock in the checkpoint gains by converting the temporary queue marshals into a weekend flex team through Thanksgiving and keeping the 25-minute peak from rebounding. For on-time performance, sequence Taxiway Kilo maintenance in two-hour night blocks and require carriers using Gates D2-D6 to pre-file swap plans with the AOC by 2100 the prior day. Sustain and extend the $12.02 revenue result by making the cruise-transfer retail package permanent for sail days and adding wayfinding from baggage claim to the offer points.

periods.analysis: The year-end picture is red because the reliability trend is now persistent, not episodic. Annual enplaned passengers recovered by 876,799, from 16,518,486 to 17,395,285, but stayed yellow and short of the 18,000,000 mark. On-time performance slipped again from 71.5% to 70.9%, red, and TSA/CBP peak wait time worsened from 25 minutes to 29 minutes as holiday charter activity and international bank bunching overloaded the same staffing windows we identified last year. Non-aeronautical revenue per enplanement rose from $12.02 to $12.50, green, matching the prior holiday high without masking the operating risk.
periods.recommendations: Do not normalize a 70.9% on-time airport; direct airlines and ground handlers to a corrective action table by carrier, delay code, and gate zone within 30 days. Pre-clear the holiday international bank plan with CBP by staffing window, including contingency use of secondary booths when queue length reaches the glass wall at FIS east. Sustain the $12.50 revenue performance by extending premium parking pre-booking and holiday retail kiosks, while assigning curb officers to keep commercial shuttles from interfering with terminal flow.

periods.analysis: Demand is back above target, but the passenger promise is still not where I will accept it. Annual enplaned passengers increased by 956,084, from 17,395,285 to 18,351,369, turning green above the 18,000,000 target. On-time performance fell from 70.9% to 70.4%, red, and TSA/CBP peak wait time worsened from 29 minutes to 32 minutes, red, repeating the prior Q1 stress pattern during spring-break and international arrival peaks. Non-aeronautical revenue per enplanement declined from $12.50 to $12.24 but remained green and well above the $10.50 target.
periods.recommendations: Shift the reliability program from voluntary coordination to operating requirements: include turn-time compliance, gate-readiness, and baggage make-up performance in the airline quarterly review letters. Put a spring-break surge plan in place by lane and booth, with TSA canine support requested for the 0500 wave and CBP overtime assigned to the Sunday international bank. Sustain green revenue by keeping premium parking inventory open for reservation customers, but cap oversell so revenue does not create curb and garage congestion.

periods.analysis: The second quarter shows some queue recovery, but the overall objective remains red because on-time performance is still moving against us. Annual enplaned passengers decreased by 819,003, from 18,351,369 to 17,532,366, returning to yellow and below the 18,000,000 target. On-time performance declined from 70.4% to 70%, red against the 80% target, while TSA/CBP peak wait time improved from 32 minutes to 28 minutes, yellow but still eight minutes above standard. Non-aeronautical revenue per enplanement fell from $12.24 to $11.72, still green, indicating a healthy commercial base but less cushion as passenger volumes softened.
periods.recommendations: Hold the line on the checkpoint improvement by making the lane-opening dashboard a weekly executive review item until peak wait time is at or below 20 minutes. For on-time performance, prioritize the summer airfield playbook: protect pushback windows on Taxiways Kilo and Mike, stage spare tugs at D5 and C11, and require recovery crews for the last two inbound banks. Sustain the $11.72 revenue result by refreshing garage pre-booking and local concessions offers for summer travelers, while using the softer quarter to renegotiate delivery routes that reduce terminal conflicts.

periods.analysis: Passenger volume returned just above target and peak waits improved, but on-time performance remains 72% against an 80% target. Commercial revenue is still above target despite a further decline per passenger. Reliability therefore remains the controlling gap for this objective.
periods.recommendations: Prioritize a carrier-backed first-wave recovery plan while sustaining checkpoint staffing triggers and monitoring the narrow passenger and revenue margins.
